title: Chapter 99: Hensheng: To Hate Life 2
content:
Chapter 99

Jin Ling sneakily cut his eyes toward Wei Wuxian again. Now that the dog was nowhere in sight, Wei Wuxian finally managed to drag his scattered wits back into his skull. Rubbing his temples, he groaned, "Kid, what on earth were you thinking, roaming around with a dog in the dead of night all on your own?"

What he didn't know was that after he’d slipped away from Lotus Pier by boat with Lan Wangji and Wen Ning, Jin Ling had secretly gone looking for him. Finding him gone without a trace, Jin Ling had completely lost his temper at his uncle—who had been losing his mind, cornering every passerby and forcing them to draw some rusty sword. Jin Ling had jabbed a finger right at Jiang Cheng’s face, screaming that it was entirely his fault Wei Wuxian had run off, only to get smacked straight into the dirt for his insolence. Thoroughly unhinged, Jin Ling decided that if his uncle wouldn’t help, he’d track Wei Wuxian down himself with Fairy.

The spiritual hound hadn't disappointed, tracking Wei Wuxian’s scent straight to the vicinity of the Guanyin Temple. But the second Jin Ling had knocked on the front gate, Fairy caught the sharp scent of murderous intent lurking within. The hound had spun around on a dime, latching onto his sleeve and barking bloody murder to pull him back. Unfortunately, the temple looked so suspicious that Jin Ling figured even if Wei Wuxian wasn't inside, he had to see what was going on. In the end, he walked straight into the lion's den.

Naturally, Jin Ling wasn't about to admit any of that. He just crossed his arms and scoffed.

Jin Guangyao led the rest of the men into the courtyard. Just as the heavy gates were about to swing shut, he glanced back over his shoulder. "Where's the spiritual hound?"

A monk bowed low. "The black-maned hound is vicious to a fault, biting anyone who gets close. We failed our task, Sect Leader—it slipped away."

"Hunt it down and kill it," Jin Guangyao ordered, voice smooth and chillingly calm. "That beast is far too clever. If it leads people here, it’ll complicate things."

"Understood!"

The monk drew his blade and slipped out, and the gates slammed shut behind him. Jin Ling’s eyes widened in disbelief. "You're actually going to kill it? You were the one who gave Fairy to me!"

Jin Guangyao didn't answer. Instead, he tilted his head. "A-Ling, what brought you all the way out here?"

Jin Ling stole a glance at Wei Wuxian, hesitating.

Before he could answer, Lan Xichen spoke up from the courtyard. "Jin-zongzhu. Jin Ling is still only a child."

Jin Guangyao met his gaze. "I am well aware."

"He is also your nephew," Lan Xichen pressed, his tone heavy.

Jin Guangyao let out a dry, helpless laugh. "Er-ge, what are you imagining? Of course I know he’s a child, and of course I know he's my nephew. What do you think I'm going to do—slit his throat to silence him?"

Lan Xichen maintained a stony silence. Jin Guangyao gave a gentle shake of his head, turning back to Jin Ling. "You heard him, A-Ling. If you run around or scream, who knows what terrible things I might have to do to you. Be a good boy and behave."

Jin Ling had always been close with this little uncle of his. Jin Guangyao had spoiled him rotten for as long as he could remember, and even now, the man's smile was warm and amiable. Yet under the circumstances, Jin Ling couldn't bring himself to look at him the same way anymore. He quietly shuffled over to stand beside Wei Wuxian and Lan Xichen, looking surprisingly well-behaved.

Jin Guangyao turned his back on them. "Haven't they unearthed it yet? Tell the men inside to pick up the pace!"

"Yes, sir!" Another monk bolted toward the main hall, blade drawn.

Only then did Wei Wuxian register the relentless, muffled scrape of shovels and shifting stone echoing from the deepest sanctuary. It sounded like an army of men excavating something massive.What in the world is he digging up? An escape tunnel? The Yin Tiger Tally? Or whatever's being held down by that suppression array?

"Come to think of it, I haven't asked," Jin Guangyao called out, turning to face him. "How did Master Wei happen upon this place? Please don't tell me you and Hanguang-jun were simply taking in the scenery and stumbled across it by chance."

Wei Wuxian countered easily, "Lianfang-zun tucked a rather conspicuous property deed right beside my old manuscripts in the Fragrance Palace. Have you forgotten already?"

"Ah," Jin Guangyao sighed with mild regret. "Careless of me. I really should have kept them in separate places."

Wei Wuxian shrugged. "Well, seeing as we're entirely at your mercy right now, could Lianfang-zun satisfy a little curiosity? What exactly are you keeping pinned beneath this temple?"

Jin Guangyao smiled, eyes crinkling. "Curiosity carries quite a hefty price tag. Are you sure you want to pay it, Master Wei?"

"Oh," Wei Wuxian drawled. "In that case, I think I'll pass for now."

Lan Xichen stepped up beside him. It was only then that Wei Wuxian noticed Shuoyue was drawn an inch from its scabbard—yet the blade was entirely dead, devoid of any humming spiritual light.

Startled, Wei Wuxian asked, "Zewu-jun, what happened to you?"

Lan Xichen lowered his eyes, shame coloring his voice. "I was a fool. I allowed myself to be deceived and walked straight into a trap. My spiritual energy is completely blocked. Even with Shuoyue and Liebing at my side, I am useless."

"There's no shame in that," Wei Wuxian said, waving it off. "Spinning lies has always been Lianfang-zun's finest craft."

Remembering what he'd witnessed through Empathy—Meng Yao feigning suicide to stab Nie Mingjue in the back—and pairing it with the recent rumors that Lianfang-zun had been "gravely wounded," it took zero effort to deduce exactly how Lan Xichen had been swindled out of his golden core's power.

Jin Guangyao turned to a cluster of monks, barking brisk orders: "Set up a warding array. When Hanguang-jun arrives, hold him off for as long as you can."

Wei Wuxian frowned. "What makes you so sure Hanguang-jun is coming at all?"

His mind raced, debating whether spinning a bluff might make Jin Guangyao drop his guard. But Jin Guangyao seemed to read him like an open book, smiling faintly. "Of course he'll come. Since Master Wei has caught the scent of this temple, there's no way Hanguang-jun doesn't know something is off. Surely you didn't think I’d buy it if you claimed he wasn't by your side?"

Wei Wuxian clicked his tongue. "Sharp as ever."

Lan Xichen turned to him, brow furrowed. "Master Wei, if Wangji is nearby, why isn't he with you?"

"We split up," Wei Wuxian said smoothly.

Lan Xichen blinked, caught off guard. "I was told you were injured coming down from the Burial Mounds. Why on earth would he leave your side under those circumstances?"

Wei Wuxian narrowed his eyes. "Who told you that?"

"I did," Jin Guangyao supplied cheerfully.

Wei Wuxian shot him a dry look before turning back to Lan Xichen. "Look, it's like this: I couldn't sleep tonight, so I went for a stroll outside the inn. Stumbled across this place entirely by accident. Hanguang-jun is sleeping in a separate room; he has no idea I slipped out."

Jin Guangyao raised an eyebrow, genuinely surprised. "You two took separate rooms?"

Wei Wuxian bristled. "Who told you we'd share one?"

Jin Guangyao simply smiled, keeping his lips sealed.

Wei Wuxian groaned. "Right, got it."Lan Xichen told him.He shook his head. "You two really tell each other everything, don't you?"

Lan Xichen, however, wasn't remotely amused. "Master Wei, did something happen between you two?"

The gentle warmth that usually graced his features vanished, replaced by an ironclad gravity that made him look uncannily like Lan Wangji. Wei Wuxian couldn't fathom why the man was reacting so intensely.

Feeling a sudden pinch of guilt, he deflected, "Lan-zongzhu, what could possibly happen between us? Shouldn't we be focusing on dealing with him first?"

He cut his eyes toward Jin Guangyao, but Lan Xichen merely sighed. "My apologies. I spoke out of turn."

Jin Guangyao laughed softly. "Oh, something definitely happened. Something significant, by the looks of it."

Wei Wuxian sneered, "The entire cultivation world is mobilizing to hunt you down, Lianfang-zun. You really have the luxury to stand around gossiping about other people's business? Feeling a bit chatty tonight, are we?"

"Perish the thought," Jin Guangyao replied smoothly. "I merely find it bittersweet. Hanguang-jun has waited in bitter devotion for so many agonizing years, only to find himself still kept at arm's length. Lan-zongzhu isn't the only one who feels anxious for him; even an outsider like me can't help but ache on his behalf."

Wei Wuxian’s head snapped toward him. "What bitter devotion? Kept at arm's length from what?"

At that, both Jin Guangyao and Lan Xichen froze in utter astonishment. The two of them stared at him, scouring his face as if trying to decipher whether he was deliberately playing dumb.

A violent jolt tore through Wei Wuxian’s chest. Something that had withered and died hours ago in that ruined room suddenly began clawing its way back to life, desperate and trembling. Forcing his voice to stay level, he demanded, "What the hell do you mean by that?"

Jin Guangyao tilted his head. "What do I mean? Master Wei, are you truly this dense, or are you just pretending? Because whether it's genuine or an act, if Hanguang-jun were here to hear you say that, it would break his heart."

"I genuinely don't understand!" Wei Wuxian shouted, losing his grip. "Spit it out!"

Lan Xichen looked at him, completely floored. "Master Wei, do not tell me that after being at Wangji's side for this long, you are entirely oblivious to his feelings?"

Wei Wuxian lunged forward, grabbing Lan Xichen’s sleeve so hard he nearly dropped to his knees. "Lan-zongzhu! Lan-zongzhu, please! What feelings?! Are you saying... could it be...?"

Lan Xichen violently yanked his arm free, his expression twisting with horrified disbelief. "You truly had no idea? Then have you already forgotten how those discipline whip scars on his back came to be? Did you not see the brand seared into his chest?!"

"The discipline whip?!" Wei Wuxian grabbed him again, his voice cracking. "Lan-zongzhu, I swear to you, I don't know! Tell me! Please, just tell me how he got those scars! Do they... do they have something to do with me?!"

A flush of raw anger broke through Lan Xichen’s composure. "If they have nothing to do with you, do you honestly believe he mutilated himself for sport?!"

Zewu-jun was celebrated across the realm for his unshakable grace, but the moment Lan Wangji was involved, his temper flared hot and real. Yet taking in the sheer, unvarnished torment on Wei Wuxian’s face, his fury cooled just enough to give way to doubt. "Did you... suffer memory loss?"

"My memory?" Wei Wuxian raked his brain, frantically clawing through the past. "I don't remember losing any part of my—wait."

There was a blank. One single, gaping hole in his mind.

The Bloodbath of the Nightless City.

That night, believing Wen Qing and Wen Ning had already been reduced to scattered ash, cornered by the self-righteous crusade of the great clans, and watching Jiang Yanli bleed out right before his eyes, he had lost his mind. He’d pieced the Yin Tiger Tally together and unleashed an indiscriminate slaughter. The dead reanimated by the tally slaughtered the living, and the newly fallen rose as fresh corpses, forging an endless, self-sustaining meat grinder that turned the ruins into a living hell.

Afterward, though he had somehow managed to stay on his feet and vaguely remembered stumbling away from that abattoir, his consciousness had unraveled into a black fog. By the time his wits returned, he was already sitting dazed and hollow at the foot of the Burial Mounds, days later.

Lan Xichen watched him closely. "Do you remember now?"

"The Nightless City...?" Wei Wuxian whispered, his voice shaking. "I... I always thought I dragged myself back through the woods in a daze. Could it be...?"

Lan Xichen let out a bitter, exasperated laugh. "Master Wei! How many cultivators stood against you that night? Three thousand men! No matter how peerless your genius, do you truly believe you could have walked away from that bloodbath entirely unscathed on your own? It's impossible!"

Wei Wuxian choked out, "Lan Zhan... what did Lan Zhan do?"

"If you don't remember what he did, I know for a fact he would take it to his grave before ever uttering a word to you," Lan Xichen said, his tone heavy and unrelenting. "And you would never ask. Fine. Let me be the one to tell you."

He took a step forward. "That night, you merged the two halves of the Yin Tiger Tally. Once the slaughter ended, you were completely spent. Wangji had been struck down by your own hand during your rampage; his condition was barely any better than yours, propped up only by the steel of Bichen. Yet the moment he saw you stumble into the dark, he went after you without a second's hesitation.

"Hardly anyone left on that field was still conscious, and I was entirely paralyzed. I could do nothing but watch, helpless, as Wangji—his spiritual reserves bled dry—limped desperately through the carnage, caught you in his arms, hauled you onto Bichen, and took flight.

"It took two full hours for my spiritual energy to recover enough for me to fly back to Gusu and rally reinforcements. I was terrified that if the other sects tracked you down first, Wangji would be branded your accomplice—ruining his name forever at best, or cut down on the spot without trial at worst. My uncle and I handpicked thirty-three respected elders who had always held Wangji in the highest esteem. We scoured the realm in secret for two days straight before finally locating your trail in Yiling.

"Wangji had hidden you inside a cavern. When we breached the entrance, you were sitting blankly upon a stone, entirely out of your mind. Wangji was holding your hand, pouring his spiritual energy into your meridians, speaking to you softly, over and over again.

"And from beginning to end, you had only one word for him.

"You screamed at him toget lost."

Wei Wuxian’s throat closed up, his eyes burning scarlet, utterly robbed of speech.

Lan Xichen continued, relentless: "My uncle stepped out before him, furiously demanding an explanation. Wangji acted as though he had known we would find him all along. He simply said there was nothing to explain; it was as it appeared.

"In all his life, he had never once spoken back to my uncle or to me. Yet for your sake, Wangji not only defied him—he drew his blade against his own kin! He fought the very elders of Gusu Lan, striking down all thirty-three of the seniors we brought, leaving them gravely wounded..."

Wei Wuxian buried his face in his hands, clutching at his hair. "...I didn't... I swear I didn't know... I really..."

He had nothing else to offer, reduced to repeating that he didn't know over and over again like a broken record.

Lan Xichen swallowed his ache, forcing the rest out: "Thirty-three lashes from the discipline whip! Handed down in a single sentencing—one strike for every elder he struck. You ought to know how much agony that weapon inflicts, how many months a man must lie half-dead just to survive it! After he stubbornly dragged you back to the Burial Mounds, he returned to the Cloud Recesses in silence to accept his judgment. Do you have any idea how long he knelt before the Wall of Discipline?!

"When I went to see him, I told him,'Master Wei has committed an unforgivable catastrophe. Why must you throw your own life into the fire alongside his?'And do you know what he told me? He said he could not judge whether what you did was right or wrong. But whether right or wrong, he was willing to shoulder every consequence by your side.

"Those years of 'seclusion' were nothing of the sort—he was simply too broken to stand! And even then, the moment news of your death reached Gusu, he dragged that battered, shattered body out of bed and forced his way to the Burial Mounds, desperate just to catch one last glimpse of the ashes...

"Back in that cave, the way he spoke to you, the way he looked at you—a blind, deaf mute would have understood the depth of his devotion! That was why my uncle was so entirely beside himself with rage. Since he was a child, Wangji was the paragon of our clan, the jewel of the cultivation world. Pristine, upright, untainted by a speck of dust. The single mistake he has ever made in his entire life wasyou!

"And yet you stand there... and say you didn't know? Master Wei, after returning to this world, how many times have you confessed your supposed love to him? How relentlessly have you clung to his side? Every single night... sharing a bed with him... And now you claim you had no idea?! If you truly felt nothing, why on earth did you do all those things?!"

Wei Wuxian wanted nothing more than to tear his own throat out.

It was precisely because he hadn't known that he’d had the audacity to pull those stunts!

A bone-deep terror settled into his marrow. If Lan Wangji had never realized that Wei Wuxian had forgotten those days following the Nightless City... if Lan Wangji had spent all this time believing Wei Wuxian had known his heart all along... then what had all his shameless antics looked like since his return?

In the beginning, he had acted like a crude, repulsive cut-sleeve specifically to disgust Lan Wangji, desperate to get thrown out of the Cloud Recesses so they could go their separate ways. Lan Wangji couldn't possibly have missed how superficial that act was. And yet... he had still insisted on keeping Wei Wuxian shielded by his side, refusing to let Jiang Cheng lay a finger on him. Answering every question, indulging every whim, swallowing every insult, showing boundless, unconditional patience. Even when subjected to Wei Wuxian’s relentless, borderline cruel teasing, the man had held himself to immaculate restraint, never crossing the line.

Then what about earlier, back at the inn?

When Lan Wangji had violently shoved him away after waking up... had it been because he thought Wei Wuxian was just toying with him on another reckless, cruel whim?

Wei Wuxian couldn't bear to think another second.

He spun on his heel and bolted for the gates. Half a dozen cultivators lunged to block his path, and Jin Guangyao called out, "Master Wei, I can appreciate your agitation—"

Wei Wuxian couldn't care less. All he wanted was to sprint back to the inn, throw himself at Lan Wangji’s feet, and spill his guts out in a desperate, tangled confession. Cracking a concussive palm strike straight into the chests of two monks trying to grab him, he roared, "You don't understand shit!"

The blow knocked the monks off their feet, but instantly, seven or eight more swarmed in to pin him down. Darkness flickered at the edges of Wei Wuxian’s vision.

Jin Guangyao casually finished his sentence from the courtyard: "...I merely wanted to tell you that there's no need to rush. Your Hanguang-jun is already here."

A blinding arc of ice-blue sword-glare cleaved through the heavens. With a razor-sharp shriek, Bichen descended like falling frost, scattering the circle of cultivators surrounding Wei Wuxian in an instant before snapping cleanly back into its master's grip.

Lan Wangji touched down silently outside the sanctuary. He cast a single look toward Wei Wuxian—his expression as calm and unreadable as ever.

The sight made Wei Wuxian’s chest seize so violently it felt like a physical cramp. Every confession, every frantic plea he’d been screaming inside his head crumbled into dust, knotting uselessly in his throat.

All he could manage was a broken whisper: "...Lan Zhan."

Jin Ling had been standing there, utterly floored by Lan Xichen’s revelation. Seeing Lan Wangji arrive was an immense relief, but catching the look exchanged between the two men, the boy's expression soured into something deeply unsettled.

Jin Guangyao sighed softly. "See? What did I tell you? Where Master Wei goes, Hanguang-jun is sure to follow."

Lan Wangji’s knuckles tightened on Bichen’s hilt, his posture shifting forward to strike.

Jin Guangyao chuckled. "Hanguang-jun, I’d suggest you take five paces back."

A sudden, needle-sharp prick of pain bit into Wei Wuxian’s throat.

Lan Xichen called out in a frantic whisper, "Careful! Do not move!"

Lan Wangji’s gaze locked onto Wei Wuxian’s neck, the color draining from his face until he was ghost-white.

Tied taut against Wei Wuxian’s throat was an impossibly thin, pale golden guqin string.
